evidenceAudit.scope: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) and diabetic macular oedema (DME) in India: screening, grading, referral, follow-up, fitness for intervention and treatment at tertiary level, built on the ICMR Diabetic Retinopathy STW (July 2020).
findings: Screening at diagnosis of diabetes and at least yearly, DR grades (no DR, mild, moderate and severe NPDR, PDR), DME grades, referral of moderate NPDR or worse and moderate DME or worse (any DR if seen by a non-ophthalmologist), urgent referral triggers, surgical indications, fitness thresholds (BP 150/90 mmHg or lower; fasting glucose below 140, post-prandial below 180 mg/dL) and pre-operative povidone-iodine preparation checked against the ICMR DR STW (July 2020).
Annual dilated fundoscopy from the ICMR Type 2 Diabetes STW.
unverifiedSections: Anti-VEGF drug doses, laser parameters and intravitreal steroid use are not in the ICMR workflow; treatment is specialist and not dosed here.
Screening intervals for type 1 diabetes and pregnancy are not in the opened workflow.
HbA1c and lipid targets are not in the DR workflow; see the Type 2 diabetes topic.
Drug cautions, contraindications and renal or hepatic adjustment lines without a source tag are general pharmacology statements and need formulary confirmation.

pathophysiology.summary: Diabetic retinopathy is a leading cause of preventable blindness in India, where diabetes is very common and often diagnosed late. Chronic hyperglycaemia damages retinal capillaries, causing microaneurysms, haemorrhages and leakage (non-proliferative DR), then capillary closure and ischaemia that drive new vessel growth (proliferative DR), with risk of vitreous haemorrhage and retinal detachment. Diabetic macular oedema can reduce vision at any stage. Vision is often normal until late, so every person with diabetes needs retinal screening at diagnosis and at least yearly (ICMR STW). Laser, intravitreal injections and vitreoretinal surgery at tertiary level prevent most severe vision loss if given in time.
keyMechanisms: Hyperglycaemia damages pericytes and capillary endothelium.
Leaky capillaries and microaneurysms cause haemorrhages, exudates and macular oedema.
Capillary closure causes retinal ischaemia and VEGF release.
VEGF drives new fragile vessels that bleed and scar (proliferative DR).

symptoms: Floaters or sudden vision loss (vitreous haemorrhage)
physicalSigns: New vessels at disc or elsewhere
redFlags: Hard exudates or haemorrhages near the macula (ICMR STW)
Non-dilating pupil, blurred disc margins, no fundal view, absent foveal reflex (ICMR STW)

differentials.distinguishingFeatures: Arteriolar narrowing, flame haemorrhages, disc swelling; high BP.
Blurred vision with lens opacity; normal fundus.
Drusen; older age; no diabetic changes elsewhere.

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: More than microaneurysms but less than severe NPDR.
Intraretinal haemorrhages 20 or more in each quadrant, definite venous beading in 2 quadrants, or IRMA in 1 quadrant, without proliferative signs.
Neovascularisation or vitreous or preretinal haemorrhage.
Mild: outside central subfield; moderate: within central subfield, not centre; severe: involving the centre.

clinicalManagement.title: Screen
clinicalManagement.timeframe: At diabetes diagnosis, then at least yearly
actions: Retinal screening when diabetes is detected (ICMR STW).
Repeat yearly, or more often by grade (ICMR STW).

clinicalManagement.title: Refer
actions: Moderate NPDR or worse, or moderate DME or worse: retina specialist (ICMR STW).
Urgent: vision loss, macular exudates or haemorrhages, rubeosis, no fundal view (ICMR STW).

clinicalManagement.title: Treat at tertiary level
actions: Intravitreal injections, laser photocoagulation or vitreoretinal surgery at tertiary level (ICMR STW).
Surgery for sudden vision loss, clinically significant macular oedema, rubeosis or PDR (ICMR STW).

clinicalManagement.title: Prepare for intervention
actions: BP 150/90 mmHg or lower; fasting glucose below 140, post-prandial below 180 mg/dL (ICMR STW).
Topical broad-spectrum antibiotic four times daily for 1–3 days; 10% povidone-iodine to the lids and 5% in the conjunctival sac (ICMR STW).

clinicalManagement.title: Systemic control
actions: Optimise glucose, BP and lipids with the diabetes team (see Type 2 diabetes and Hypertension topics).

branches.label: Specialist treatment
branches.entryCriteria: Moderate NPDR or worse, or DME, managed by a retina specialist (no medicine dosed here).

medicationPlan.note: No medicine is dosed in this topic: the ICMR workflow places intravitreal and laser treatment at tertiary level without doses. Systemic drugs for glucose and BP are in their own topics. India-only topic; the Saudi topic is unchanged. Not clinically reviewed.

keyPoints: Refer moderate NPDR or worse, and moderate DME or worse.
Vision loss or rubeosis: urgent referral.
Control BP and glucose before surgery.
pitfalls: Losing patients to follow-up after laser.
